title: Skin Diversity: Integrating Basic and Applied Science with Medical Education to Address a Long-Standing Problem in Diagnosis and the Representativeness of Scientific Findings
summary: Non-invasive techniques are used to gather information on skin color, which improves the diagnosis of skin diseases and, consequently, medical education, diagnosis, artificial intelligence, basic research, and product development. Depending on skin pigmentation, non-invasive techniques for skin assessment may behave differently. This makes it difficult to evaluate the physiology and pathophysiology of the skin.

interventions.name: A study involving 36 participants, 6 per phototype, will be conducted. In an initial classification, the phototype classification will be used, as this has been the most commonly used approach in previous studies. Measurements will be taken using various non-invasive examination methods: laser scann

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
-    have been informed about the study's objectives and the nature of the procedures
-    have provided written informed consent.
Exclusion criteria:
-    Participants who have suffered burns or other damage to hairless skin,
-    Pregnant women and nursing mothers,
-    Individuals with a skin condition that could interfere with the conduct of an experiment in this study.
-    Participants who have not provided written informed consent or who have not given their written informed consent after receiving an explanation,
-    Individuals who are unable to make decisions on their own behalf.
